about: Authored countries a generated world may hold, each where its requirements fit: beyond a march on the side named, of a country of one of the terrains named. The first march a company reaches where one fits leads into it instead of a country drawn from the seed; each is placed once in a world (src/world/frontier.ts). Of the countries among one kind (the independent adventures), a world holds only the one its seed chooses. Each says what the folk of the first region say of it (rumour, with {keeper} the innkeeper of the town the road leaves from), and what the company knows of it once told (heard).

countries.name: Merrowdale
countries.rumour: 'Up the north road there is Merrowdale,' says {keeper}. 'There is a long ridge across the head of the dale, and they say a giant king is buried under it. Something tall walks the crest at night. The steward has posted forty crowns to have it laid.'
countries.heard: Up the north road lies Merrowdale, where a giant king is said to be buried under the long ridge, and something tall walks its crest at night.

countries.name: Thrume
countries.rumour: 'East over the march, under the fells, there is a salt town, Saltgrave,' says {keeper}. 'People pay to sleep there, and some of them do not come home. And the giants have come down off the mountain, they say, for the first time anyone remembers.'
countries.heard: East over the march lies Saltgrave, a salt town under the fells, where people pay to sleep and some do not come home, and the giants have come down off the mountain.

countries.name: the Strewnfield
countries.rumour: 'South, in the Strewnfield,' says {keeper}, 'a room of glass fell into a barley field by Cobble Ring. It grows, they say, wherever nobody is watching it. They sit up with it all night on stools.'
countries.heard: South over the march lies the Strewnfield, where a room of glass fell into a barley field by Cobble Ring, and grows wherever nobody watches it.

countries.name: the Corrow
countries.rumour: 'West of here is the Corrow,' says {keeper}. 'There is a mountain hangs over it in the sky, on a chain, and they say it is drifting. And there is a well there nobody has been to the bottom of.'
countries.heard: West over the march lies the Corrow, where a mountain hangs in the sky on a chain, drifting, over a well nobody has been to the bottom of.

countries.name: the Ghessil Uplands
countries.rumour: 'West, up on the Ghessil Uplands,' says {keeper}, 'there is a light lies on the glass that slows whatever drinks it. There are people standing in it, they say, that went in last autumn and are standing there yet, alive.'
countries.heard: West over the march lie the Ghessil Uplands, where a light on the glass slows whatever drinks it, and people stand in it alive since last autumn.

countries.name: the Ossel delta
countries.rumour: 'Down the east road, where the marsh meets the sea, there's Tessary on the Ossel,' says {keeper}. 'Their legions came home from the war a week back, and they say some of the soldiers are getting up in the night and walking into the sea. Barefoot, in step, eyes open. An eel-wife there has put up a notice: she'll give her savings to anyone who can tell her where her boy went.'
countries.heard: East over the march lies Tessary on the Ossel, where the legions have come home from the war and some of the soldiers walk into the sea at night; an eel-wife there offers her savings for news of her son.
